children: At the upper end of the price band, NSE seeks a valuation of around Rs 4.42 lakh crore

The much-awaited initial public offering of the National Stock Exchange of India (NSE) opened for subscription on Thursday, September 17, marking the stock market operator’s long-awaited entry into the listed market.

The Rs 22,561.57 crore IPO will remain open until September 21. The issue comprises an offer for sale (OFS) of up to 12.64 crore equity shares, with no fresh issue. As a result, NSE will not receive any proceeds from the public offer, with the entire amount going to existing shareholders selling their stakes.

NSE has fixed the price band at Rs 1,700-1,785 per share. The lot size is eight shares, taking the minimum retail investment to Rs 14,280 at the upper end of the price band. The issue has reserved up to 50 per cent for qualified institutional buyers, 15 per cent for non-institutional investors and 35 per cent for retail investors.

At the upper end of the price band, NSE is seeking a valuation of around Rs 4.42 lakh crore. The shares are scheduled to be listed on the BSE on September 24, with allotment expected to be finalised on September 22.

Ahead of the public issue, NSE raised around Rs 6,746 crore from anchor investors through an allocation of shares at Rs 1,785 apiece. The anchor book included large domestic and global institutional investors, with Life Insurance Corporation of India emerging as the largest anchor investor. Norway’s Government Pension Fund, Abu Dhabi Investment Authority and Fidelity were among other investors participating in the anchor allocation.

The OFS includes shares held by existing investors such as State Bank of India, Canada Pension Plan Investment Board, Aranda Investments (Mauritius), New India Assurance Company, SBI Capital Markets, Stock Holding Corporation of India, Bank of Baroda, United India Insurance Company and General Insurance Corporation of India.

NSE remains one of India’s largest market infrastructure institutions, with its business spanning cash equities, equity derivatives, currency derivatives, debt markets, market data, indices and clearing services.

On a consolidated basis, NSE reported profit after tax of Rs 10,302 crore in FY26, compared with Rs 12,188 crore in FY25 and Rs 8,306 crore in FY24. Operating EBITDA stood at Rs 11,098 crore in FY26, against Rs 12,647 crore in FY25 and Rs 9,870 crore in FY24.

The exchange’s financial performance remains closely linked to trading activity, particularly derivatives volumes. The company has also been seeking to diversify revenue through areas such as data, indices and technology-led services.

The IPO is being managed by a consortium of 20 book-running lead managers. They include Kotak Mahindra Capital Company, JM Financial, Morgan Stanley India, Citigroup Global Markets India, HSBC Securities and Capital Markets (India), JP Morgan India, SBI Capital Markets, Anand Rathi Advisors, Avendus Capital, Axis Capital, DAM Capital Advisors, Equirus Capital, HDFC Bank, ICICI Securities, IDBI Capital Markets & Securities, IIFL Capital Services, Motilal Oswal Investment Advisors, Nuvama Wealth Management, Pantomath Capital Advisors and 360 ONE WAM.
MUFG Intime India is the registrar to the issue.

The NSE IPO is among India’s largest public offerings and comes after several years of regulatory and procedural delays surrounding the exchange’s proposed listing. The public issue now gives investors an opportunity to participate in the ownership of the country’s largest stock exchange, while also placing greater focus on its valuation, trading-volume dependence and future earnings trajectory.
